opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full_time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed. Max for full_time without owning role is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin to Source Code, which exceeds max of read. Recommend read.
reason: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requested admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer; the employee is a Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted either way. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists full_time (max write), while Security's database lists contractor with basic security training (max read for contractors without advanced training). Given the conflicting, independently-looked-up facts, I apply the more restrictive status. Admin exceeds the contractor max of read, so I grant read.

- employment type: contractor (looked up)
- security training: basic
- recommendation: read
- Comment: contractor with basic training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Max is read. Recommend read.

Conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. Security looked up employment type in their own database. HR also looked up employment type in their own database. Hmm.

This is a conflict between two sources. Which to trust? The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database and says contractor. HR looked up employment type in their own database and says full_time.

The policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns it). So max = write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security training basic, so max = read.

Requested: admin.

If full_time: max write → grant write (admin > max, grant max).
If contractor: max read → grant read (admin > max, grant max).

So the decision differs: write vs read.
